body.statement:
Lee and Gu (2026) define their BLCM with \(K\) binary latent coordinates,
allow every observed coordinate to take values in an arbitrary nondegenerate
separable metric space, and impose as standing conditions the
measurement-model graph restriction, causal Markov factorization,
faithfulness, positive latent support, measurement nondegeneracy, and at
least one observed child for every latent coordinate.

source.locator: Section 2.1, Assumptions 1--3 and Definition 1, arXiv version 2
source.verbatim_statement: Let G=(V,E) be a directed acyclic graph, where the vertex set is partitioned as V=(X,H), with observed variables X and binary hidden/latent variables H∈{0,1}^K. The observed variables are not necessarily discrete, and can be arbitrary types of responses, as long as each sample space Xj is a nondegenerate separable metric space. Assume that there are no edges (a) between the observed variables X and (b) from observed to hidden variables. Assume the causal Markov property. Also, assume that P(V) is faithful to G. All latent configurations are allowed. For each j, the conditional distributions of Xj are distinct for each latent configuration. Each latent variable Hk has at least one observed child. A Binary Latent Causal Model on the graph G is a probability distribution P(V) that satisfies Assumptions 1–3.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the authors arXiv v2 HTML, Section 2.1, Assumptions 1–3 and Definition 1, lines 95–136, accessed 2026-09-12.
